key_insight: An actively trained MTP-to-FE pipeline can predict how FLiBe-based molten salts affect heat transfer, enabling rapid screening of coolant formulations.
engineering_relevance: This framework supports reactor thermal design by linking atomistic transport properties to component-scale heat-transfer performance in molten salt systems.
method: Train Moment Tensor Potentials on ab initio data for FLiBe, FLiBe-LaF3, and FLiBe-UF4.
Run molecular dynamics to extract density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, and heat capacity over temperature/composition ranges.
Feed the transport properties into a 3D finite-element model of a linear heat exchanger to predict heat-transfer behavior.
evidence_signal: Using literature properties, the FE model matched pure FLiBe experiments within 10% in laminar flow and 18% in transitional/turbulent flow, while MTP-MD inputs overestimated heat-transfer coefficient by 25-28% and predicted an 8-11% reduction for ternary salts.
watch_item: The absolute heat-transfer reduction for FLiBe-LaF3 and FLiBe-UF4 depends on MTP accuracy, especially biases in thermal conductivity and viscosity.
paper_title: Integrating moment tensor potentials with finite-element modeling for heat transfer prediction in FLiBe-based molten salt systems
